properties.description: A bar is a retail business establishment that serves alcoholic beverages, such as beer, wine, liquor, and cocktails for consumption on the premises. Bars often also serve food and snacks to compliment the drinks. They are also social places where people get together to enjoy drinks and conversation.
properties.history: Bars have been a part of human culture for thousands of years. They serve as places for socializing, celebrating, and escaping the mundanities of everyday life. Initially, these establishments served just wine or beer, but with time, they expanded their offerings to include various spirits and cocktails. Modern bars often offer food to accompany the drinks, ranging from snacks and appetizers to full meals.

properties.description: The bar & grill restaurant genre typically refers to an establishment that serves both alcoholic beverages as well as cooked or grilled food. The menu usually includes a range of dishes including burgers, sandwiches, steaks, fish, salads and other appetizers. The atmosphere is typically casual and is often associated with good times and camaraderie.
properties.history: The concept of the bar & grill restaurant genre has its origin in the United States during the late 19th and early 20th century. The idea was to combine the leisurely activity of drinking with the dining experience.

properties.description: Barbecue refers to a method and apparatus for char grilling food in the open air, but also to a style of food often featuring smoked and slow-roasted meats, typically served with tangy or sweet sauces. The cooking style varies by region, with each having its own traditional meats and side dishes.
properties.history: The term 'barbecue' comes from the word 'barabicu' found in the language of the Taíno people of the Caribbean. The modern way of cooking barbecue originated in the southeastern United States, most notably in the ‘Pig Belt’ states such as North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Tennessee, Mississippi, Alabama, and Missouri.
